## (1) Identifiers, names, and control status

**Common name:** MDMB-4en-PINACA

**Systematic (IUPAC) and chemical names:**
- Methyl 3,3-dimethyl-2-{[1-(pent-4-en-1-yl)-1H-indazole-3-carbonyl]amino}butanoate
- Methyl 3,3-dimethyl-2-[1-(pent-4-en-1-yl)-1H-indazole-3-carboxamido]butanoate
- Methyl 3-methyl-N-[1-(pent-4-en-1-yl)-1H-indazole-3-carbonyl]valinate
- Methyl 3-methyl-N-[1-(pent-4-en-1-yl)-1H-indazole-3-carbonyl]-L-valinate ((S)-enantiomer)
- Methyl 3-methyl-N-[1-(pent-4-en-1-yl)-1H-indazole-3-carbonyl]-D-valinate ((R)-enantiomer)
- Methyl 3,3-dimethyl-2-{[1-(pent-4-en-1-yl)-1H-indazol-3-yl]formamido}butanoate
- Methyl N-{[1-(pent-4-en-1-yl)-1H-indazole-3-yl]carbonyl}-3-methylvalinate
- Methyl 2-[1-(pent-4-en-1-yl)-1H-indazole-3-carboxamido]-3,3-dimethylbutanoate
- N-(1-methoxy-3,3-dimethyl-1-oxobutan-2-yl)-1-(pent-4-en-1-yl)-1H-indazole-3-carboxamide

**Other names and code names:**
- (4-en) ABD-PINACA
- ADB-PINACA-A
- (Pentyl-4-en) MDMB-PINACA
- MDMB-PENINACA
- MDMB-PINACA N1-pentyl-4-en isomer
- 5-CL-ADB-A [sic]. The page calls this a potentially confusing code name. It says some internet retailers advertise this name for MDMB-4en-PINACA, though the IUPAC name it gives belongs to 5Cl-ADB (5Cl-MDMB-PINACA).

**CAS numbers:**
- 2504100-70-1 ((S)-enantiomer)
- 2504100-73-4 ((R)-enantiomer)

**Other identifiers:** InChI Key LWOCBHBFWNGPGM-UHFFFAOYSA-N; a SMILES string is also given.

**Molecular formula:** C20H27N3O3

**Molecular weight:** 357.45 (monoisotopic mass 357.2052)

**ATC code:** not given

**Control status:**
- **United Nations:** not controlled under the 1961 Single Convention or the 1971 Convention on Psychotropic Substances. Assessed by the WHO ECDD in October 2020; no written recommendation had been published at the time of the meeting.
- **EU:** the Commission adopted a delegated act to add the substance to the definition of a drug in the Council Framework Decision 2004/757/JHA annex.
- **National, drug control legislation:** Croatia, Cyprus, Finland, France, Italy, Latvia, Luxembourg, Poland, Sweden, the UK; Turkey.
- **National, medicines legislation:** Lithuania; Norway.
- **National, new psychoactive substance legislation:** Austria, Belgium, Germany, Hungary.
- **No national restrictive measures reported:** Bulgaria, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Greece, Ireland, Malta, the Netherlands, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain.
- **China:** unknown whether controlled.

## (2) Forms and products

**Physical forms:**
- Pure form: neat solid; colourless oil (described for the (S)-form); powder; white powder; tan and yellow/brown powder.
- Seized and collected samples: white, beige, yellow, or orange powders.
- Purity or concentration in seized powders: not reported.

**Product types:**
- Smoking mixtures (herbal plant material or tobacco, smoked or vaporised)
- E-liquids for use in e-cigarettes
- Paper, including blotters and cards, impregnated with the substance
- Powders for processing into products or for self-preparation
- Cannabis adulterated with the substance (Netherlands, reported November 2020)

**Product or brand names:**
- 'Pico Bello Extra Strong' (Germany, seized 2017; contained 5F-ADB and 5F-ADB-PINACA)
- 'Pico Bello Made In Holland' (Germany, three seizures; also contained 5F-MDMB-PICA)
- A sample sold as '5CL-ADB-A' (Germany)
- A seized sample labelled '5F-MDMB-2201' (Germany) that was actually MDMB-4en-PINACA
- 'PTC' (liquid, France; at least one sample contained the substance)
- 'Chimique' (France; two collected samples, also containing 5F-MDMB-PICA)
- 'Heavy Weight' (United States product label)

**Seizures and drug-checking findings:**
- 770 seizures reported, including about 47 kg of powder and 4.7 kg of smoking mixtures.
- Customs seized about 44 kg of powder in 2020, approximately 99% of the total powder seized.
- About 15% of police seizures occurred in prisons or other custodial settings, in at least six Member States.
- Chiral analysis of paper samples from three Scottish prisons confirmed the (S)-enantiomer.
- The substance was not reported as an active ingredient in any medicinal product.

## (3) Street and slang names

- **'Spice':** historically a common slang name for smoking mixtures containing synthetic cannabinoids in some countries, not specific to this substance.
- **'herbal smoking mixtures', 'herbal incense', 'synthetic cannabis', 'legal weed', 'K2', 'smoking mixtures':** general names for these products, with no region given.
- **'Mamba' / 'Black Mamba':** used in Birmingham, United Kingdom.
- **'magic tobacco':** used in Hungary.
- **'chimique':** used in France.
- **'Bonsai':** used in Turkey.
- **'PTC' (from 'pète ton crâne'):** liquids in France.
